core_idea: A WhatsApp-based marketplace that connects small farmers directly to urban grocery buyers, cutting out middlemen (arthis).
problem_and_inspiration: Farmers in Punjab lose 30-40% of their crop value to commission agents at the mandi. My uncle is a farmer and showed me his actual sale slips vs market price.
target_audience: Small-to-mid vegetable farmers (2-10 acres) near Lahore/Multan, and urban grocery store owners who want fresher produce at lower cost.
current_alternatives: Farmers sell exclusively through the local mandi/arthi system. Grocery owners buy through wholesalers at the mandi.
competitors_and_edge: Tazah and Farmdar are doing something similar at larger scale. We'd differentiate by being WhatsApp-only (no app download) and hyper-local to two districts first.
ideal_outcome: Every small farmer in our districts sells 80% of produce through us, getting 20% more revenue, while grocers get same-day fresh delivery at 10% lower cost than mandi.
clarity_vs_fuzzy: Clear: the core pain point and who feels it most. Fuzzy: how we handle logistics/delivery at scale, and whether farmers will trust a new middleman.
biggest_bottleneck: No logistics partner yet, and I'm non-technical so I don't know how to build the WhatsApp ordering flow.
winning_outcome: A working pilot in one district with 20 farmers and 10 grocers transacting weekly, proving the unit economics.
other_context: I'm worried about cold-chain/spoilage logistics and whether farmers will actually trust a 22-year-old over their lifelong arthi relationship.
